headline: No — cold salty corner falls short
summary: At 60 °F and 49,000 mg/L, the logged run “baseline-cold-salty-1train” reaches only 47.2% recovery and 0.539 g/L permeate salt at the documented 75.84 bar pressure cap, against the study targets of about 60% recovery and 0.5 g/L in the model. No tested operating option using the existing documented pressure, pump motor or membrane limits passes; the cheapest credible route is new higher-pressure pumping and membrane-pressure equipment, vendor-quoted and re-solved before acceptance, so this conclusion is provisional on the missing membrane projection data noted below.

assumptions: The calibrated model represents one seawater train at its design feed; plant output is five such duty trains with the sixth as spare, as documented on RO-201.

The partial second pass, stabilisation and disinfection are documented notes only and are not simulated (check_coverage for cold-salty-failing-baseline), so finished-water salt after blending, boron, stabilisation and disinfection are not proven by these runs.

Membrane area and permeability in the model are not stated in the cited study sections — the study expressly marks membrane area/flux as not stated — so the pressure/recovery result is provisional on a vendor projection at this corner.

Because E-101 is a note-only item in the model (check_coverage for cold-salty-failing-baseline), the heating conclusion is provisional on steam availability and a temperature-corrected vendor membrane projection.

highlights.text: Limits first: at 60 °F and 49,000 mg/L the second stage reaches only 0.1387 recovery against its 0.333 design check and overall recovery is 0.472 against about 0.60 (runs baseline-cold-salty-1train, ro_capacity), at the 75.84 bar pressure cap.

Already at its documented about 1,100 psig discharge cap (75.84 bar, 2004 PDF p.197); a diagnostic 95 bar run reaches 60.6% recovery but is not permitted on this pump or the existing vessels and still gives 0.529 g/L salt (run pressure-scan-95bar).

Documented steam heating (60–95 °F channel range, P&ID E-101) does not rescue the corner in the simulator — 90 °F gives 0.442 recovery (run heat-90F-per-train) — and the heater is note-only in the model, so do not rely on it without a vendor projection.
Pretreatment is two duty plus one spare 21 MGD trains (P&ID F-101); it is not the first limit found in the cold-corner runs.

Second pass is one duty plus one spare 11.1 MGD-feed train at about 90% recovery (P&ID RO-301), but it is a documented note only in this model, so finished-water quality after the partial second pass is unproven here.

Brine diffuser is documented for 16.67 MGD at 60% recovery for the 25 MGD plant (P&ID D-601); at the simulated 47.2% recovery the brine flow would be larger, which needs checking before any low-recovery workaround is accepted.

proposals.title: Add a higher-pressure feed pump train — do not uprate the existing pump
proposals.why: The existing pump is already at its documented about 1,100 psig (75.84 bar) cap while recovery is only 47.2%; a diagnostic run at 95 bar is the first point that reaches about 60% recovery, so new, properly rated pumping is required rather than a setpoint increase (runs baseline-cold-salty-1train and pressure-scan-95bar).

proposals.title: Add a higher-pressure membrane train rated for the diagnostic pressure
proposals.why: The membrane vessels and second stage are the first limit: second-stage recovery is 0.1387 against 0.333 and feed pressure is capped at 75.84 bar (run baseline-cold-salty-1train). Existing RO-201 pressure ratings must not be raised; a new rated train, fed in parallel through a splitter and recombined through a mixer, is the physical route to the 95 bar diagnostic condition, and even then permeate salt was 0.529 g/L before the unmodelled second pass, so vendor performance must be confirmed.

field_checks.item: Guaranteed membrane performance at the cold, salty corner (water permeability, salt passage and required pressure at 60% recovery)
field_checks.where: Take a full ion analysis of Brownsville Ship Channel water at IN-101 during cold, high-salinity conditions and obtain a temperature-corrected vendor membrane projection / pilot result at 60 °F and 49,000 mg/L for RO-201
field_checks.changes: Decisive: the study does not print a full ion table or membrane area/flux (data sheet, Source water and Not in the study rows), and the model's recovery, pressure and salt results all rest on assumed membrane inputs. If the vendor projection reaches 60% at or below 75.84 bar with acceptable salt, the existing trains could pass and the new high-pressure equipment proposals would not be needed; if it needs about 95 bar, the no-go conclusion stands.

field_checks.item: Steam actually available to E-101 in cold weather, and the true pressure saving from heating
field_checks.where: Confirm steam header pressure, flow and temperature on line 5001 to E-101 with the co-located power plant, and get the heating benefit from the same vendor projection above
field_checks.changes: The study credits about 1% pressure reduction per °F heated (2004 PDF p.192), but the simulator's fixed-permeability model shows heating making recovery worse (runs heat-75F/90F/95F-per-train). If verified heating plus vendor membranes bring the required pressure within 75.84 bar, heating on the existing E-101 would become the cheapest fix and displace the new-equipment proposals.

field_checks.item: Nameplate confirmation of the pump motor, turbine coupling and vessel pressure rating
field_checks.where: Field nameplates on P-201 motor, T-201 Pelton turbine and RO-201 pressure vessels
field_checks.changes: Confirms the 2,900 HP motor and about 1,100 psig class used from 2004 PDF p.197; if installed vessels or pump are in fact rated materially above 95 bar, the fix could become an operating change instead of new equipment — do not assume this.

field_checks.item: Whether finished-water quality is met after the partial second pass
field_checks.where: Confirm the required finished-water salt and any boron limit with the owner and model or pilot RO-301 at the cold-corner first-pass permeate quality
field_checks.changes: The model checks first-pass permeate against 0.5 g/L and the second pass is note-only (check_coverage); the study picks no finished-water boron limit in the cited pages. If blending after RO-301 meets the real finished-water limit, only recovery/pressure need fixing; if not, second-pass capacity or membranes must be added to the fix.

request: Can this 25 MGD concept hold about 60 percent overall recovery and the finished-water duty on the cold, salty corner of the ship-channel record (about 60 F and 49,000 mg/L TDS) with one seawater train out of service? What limits it first, and what is the cheapest way to stay at 25 MGD? Propose each change, verified in the simulator; where a limit needs new equipment, propose it as added equipment with its rating source.
